## 1) Introduction


# Things to consider :
1. How does heat stress affect yield as measured by the total weight of fruit?
2. How does heat stress affect yield as measured by the total weight of healthy fruit?
3. How does heat stress affect yield as measured by the percentage of healthy berries by count?
4. How does heat stress affect yield as measured by the percentage of healthy fruit by weight?
5. How do the cultivars, years, and intensity of the heat shocks (in the case of the acute heat
stress experiment) affect the various measures of yield?


## 2) Exploratory Data Analysis and Modifications

```{r}
data_raw <- read.csv("acute_yield_data_fall_2026.csv")

data <- data_raw %>%
                mutate(
                  year = factor(year),
                  cultivar = factor(toupper(trimws(cultivar))),
                  intensity_group = factor(toupper(trimws(intensity_group)),
                               levels = c("D", "C", "B", "A")),
                  treatment = factor(toupper(trimws(treatment)),
                               levels = c("CONTROL", "OTC"),
                               labels = c("Control", "OTC")),
                  heat_group = factor(
                                 ifelse(treatment == "Control", "Control", as.character(intensity_group)),
                                        levels = c("Control", "D", "C", "B", "A")
                                ),
                  pair_id = interaction(year, cultivar, intensity_group, plot, drop = TRUE),
                                total_weight = healthy_weight + rotten_weight,
                                healthy_count_pct = 100 * healthy_n / (healthy_n + rotten_n),
                                healthy_weight_prop = healthy_weight / total_weight,
                                healthy_weight_pct  = 100 * healthy_weight_prop,
                                pulses = as.numeric(c(A = 4, B = 3, C = 2, data = 1)[as.character(intensity_group)])
             )

# Design checks -------------------------------------------------------------
stopifnot(nrow(data) == 96, nlevels(data$pair) == 48)
stopifnot(!anyNA(data$heat_group))
stopifnot(all(data %>% count(pair_id) %>% pull(n) == 2))
stopifnot(all(data %>%
  group_by(pair_id) %>%
  summarise(ok = setequal(as.character(treatment), c("Control", "OTC")),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pull(ok)))
stopifnot(all(data$total_weight > 0), all(data$healthy_n + data$rotten_n > 0))

```

ggplot(data, aes(x = factor(heat_group), y = healthy_weight)) +

```{r }
data %>%
  transmute(`Total weight (g)` = total_weight,
            `log(total weight)` = log(total_weight)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "scale", values_to = "value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "grey70", colour = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ scale, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Count",
       title = "Total weight on the raw and log scales") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)
```

```{r design-residuals, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Absolute residuals vs fitted values from a Gaussian model. The raw scale shows a mild increase in spread with the fitted value; the log scale is flatter. This supports modelling log(total weight)."}
m_raw <- lm(total_weight ~ heat_group * year + cultivar, data = data)
m_log <- lm(log(total_weight) ~ heat_group * year + cultivar, data = data)

bind_rows(
  data.frame(fitted = fitted(m_raw), abs_resid = abs(resid(m_raw)),
             scale = "Raw scale"),
  data.frame(fitted = fitted(m_log), abs_resid = abs(resid(m_log)),
             scale = "Log scale")
) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = fitted, y = abs_resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, colour = "tomato") +
  facet_wrap(~ scale, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Fitted value", y = "|Residual|",
       title = "Absolute residuals vs fitted values: raw vs log scale") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)
```

## Pair structure

```{r design-pairs, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Control and heat total weights within the same pair are strongly correlated (r = 0.84). This supports the pair random intercept (1 | pair)."}
pair_heat <- data %>%
  filter(treatment == "OTC") %>%
  select(pair_id, heat_group)

wide <- data %>%
  select(pair_id, treatment, total_weight) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = total_weight,
              id_cols = pair_id) %>%
  left_join(pair_heat, by = "pair_id")

cor_pair <- cor(wide$Control, wide$OTC)

ggplot(wide, aes(x = Control, y = OTC, colour = heat_group)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(data = "#fee5d9", C = "#fcae91",
                                 B = "#fb6a4a", A = "#cb181d")) +
  labs(x = "Control total weight (g)", y = "Heat total weight (g)",
       colour = "Heat group",
       title = sprintf("Within-pair correlation: r = %.2f", cor_pair)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)
```


## 3) Interaction

```{r design-heat-year, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Mean total weight by heat group and year, separately for each cultivar. The 2024 and 2025 profiles differ: 2025 is lower overall, and MQ declines sharply at B/A in 2025 while ST is flatter. This supports a heat_group x year interaction."}
summ_hy <- data %>%
  group_by(heat_group, year, cultivar) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(total_weight),
            se = sd(total_weight) / sqrt(n()),
            .groups = "drop")

ggplot(summ_hy, aes(x = heat_group, y = mean, colour = year, group = year)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se), width = 0.12) +
  facet_wrap(~ cultivar) +
  labs(x = "Heat group (data = 1, C = 2, B = 3, A = 4 pulses)",
       y = "Mean total weight (g)", colour = "Year",
       title = "Heat group x year, separately by cultivar") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)
```

```{r design-heat-cultivar, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Mean total weight by heat group and cultivar, separately by year. MQ and ST differ mainly in level; their heat profiles are similar enough that a heat_group x cultivar interaction is not obviously required, but it is tested in H1."}
ggplot(summ_hy, aes(x = heat_group, y = mean, colour = cultivar, group = cultivar)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se), width = 0.12) +
  facet_wrap(~ year) +
  labs(x = "Heat group (data = 1, C = 2, B = 3, A = 4 pulses)",
       y = "Mean total weight (g)", colour = "Cultivar",
       title = "Heat group x cultivar, separately by year") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)
```

```{r design-year-cultivar, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Mean total weight by year and cultivar. The large 2025 ST drop supports a year x cultivar baseline term."}
summ_yc <- data %>%
  group_by(year, cultivar) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(total_weight),
            se = sd(total_weight) / sqrt(n()),
            .groups = "drop")

ggplot(summ_yc, aes(x = year, y = mean, colour = cultivar, group = cultivar)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se), width = 0.12) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Mean total weight (g)", colour = "Cultivar",
       title = "Year x cultivar baseline") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)
```

The figures support the following model structure:

- **log(total_weight)** rather than raw weight: the response is positive, the
  effects are naturally multiplicative, and the log-scale residuals are more
  homogeneous.
- **(1 | pair)**: control and heat plots in the same pair are strongly
  correlated, so the pair must be a random effect.
- **heat_group × year**: the 2024 and 2025 profiles have different shapes,
  especially for MQ; ST is much lower in 2025.
- **year:cultivar**: 2025 ST is much lower than 2024 ST, a baseline shift that
  is not a heat effect.
- **heat_group × cultivar**: MQ and ST differ mainly in level; their heat
  profiles are similar enough that the interaction is tested but not obviously
  required.

The model-building section below fits the candidate models H0–H4 and compares
them with AIC and likelihood-ratio tests.

## 4) How does heat stress affect yield as measured by the total weight of fruit?

```{r}
fit_lmm <- function(form) lmer(form, data = data, REML = FALSE)
# Total weight
h0_total <- fit_lmm(log(total_weight) ~ heat_group + cultivar + year + year:cultivar + (1 | pair_id))

h1_total <- fit_lmm(log(total_weight) ~ heat_group * cultivar + year + year:cultivar + (1 | pair_id))

h2_total <- fit_lmm(log(total_weight) ~ heat_group * year + cultivar + year:cultivar + (1 | pair_id))

h3_total <- fit_lmm(log(total_weight) ~ heat_group * (cultivar + year) + year:cultivar + (1 | pair_id))

h4_total <- fit_lmm(log(total_weight) ~ treatment * intensity_group + cultivar + year + year:cultivar + (1 | pair_id))

```


```{r}
aic_tab <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(Response = "Total",   Model = c("H0", "H1", "H2", "H3", "H4"),
             df = sapply(list(h0_total, h1_total, h2_total, h3_total, h4_total),
                         function(m) attr(logLik(m), "df")),
             AIC = sapply(list(h0_total, h1_total, h2_total, h3_total, h4_total), AIC)),
) %>%
  group_by(Response) %>%
  mutate(dAIC = AIC - min(AIC)) %>%
  ungroup()
kable(aic_tab)

```

We can choose h2_total, which has the smallest AIC.

We refit the selected H2 model with REML for the final estimates:

```{r h2-formula}
h2_final <- lmer(log(total_weight) ~ heat_group * year + cultivar + year:cultivar +
                   (1 | pair_id), data = data, REML = TRUE)

formula(h2_final)
```

$$
\log Y_i=\mu+\alpha_{g_i}+\beta_{t_i}+(\alpha\beta)_{g_i t_i}
+\gamma_{c_i}+(\beta\gamma)_{t_i c_i}+b_{k(i)}+\varepsilon_i,
\qquad b_k\sim N(0,\sigma_b^2),\quad \varepsilon_i\sim N(0,\sigma^2),
$$

```{r}
m1 <- glmmTMB(cbind(healthy_n, rotten_n) ~ heat_group + cultivar + factor(year) + (1 | pair_id), family = betabinomial(link = "logit"), data = data)
#summary(m1)
m2 <- glmmTMB(cbind(healthy_n, rotten_n) ~ heat_group * cultivar + factor(year) + (1 | pair_id), family = betabinomial(link = "logit"), data = data)
#summary(m2)
m3 <- glmmTMB(cbind(healthy_n, rotten_n) ~ heat_group + cultivar * factor(year) + (1 | pair_id), family = betabinomial(link = "logit"), data = data)
#summary(m3)

anova(m2, m1, m3)
```

```{r}
summary(m1)
```

```{r}
# Fixed-effect estimates
coefs <- summary(m1)$coefficients$cond

# Odds ratios
OR <- exp(coefs[, "Estimate"])

# 95% confidence intervals
CI <- exp(
  cbind(
    Lower = coefs[, "Estimate"] - 1.96 * coefs[, "Std. Error"],
    Upper = coefs[, "Estimate"] + 1.96 * coefs[, "Std. Error"]
  )
)

results <- data.frame(
  Term = rownames(coefs),
  Odds_Ratio = OR,
  CI_Lower = CI[, "Lower"],
  CI_Upper = CI[, "Upper"],
  p_value = coefs[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
)

#results
results_formatted <- results
results_formatted$Odds_Ratio <- sprintf("%.2f", results_formatted$Odds_Ratio)
results_formatted$CI_Lower   <- sprintf("%.2f", results_formatted$CI_Lower)
results_formatted$CI_Upper   <- sprintf("%.2f", results_formatted$CI_Upper)

# Format p-values (e.g., change small numbers to < 0.001)
results_formatted$p_value <- ifelse(
  results_formatted$p_value < 0.001,
  "< 0.001",
  sprintf("%.3f", results_formatted$p_value)
)

# 2. Print styled table
kable(
  results_formatted,
  col.names = c("Term", "Odds Ratio", "95% CI Lower", "95% CI Upper", "p-value"),
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Model Odds Ratios and 95% Confidence Intervals"
)

```

```{r}

```{r, echo=FALSE}
plot_heat_effects <- function(
  model,
  term_pattern = "^heat_group",
  group_map = c("A" = "4 Pulses (A)", "B" = "3 Pulses (B)", "C" = "2 Pulses (C)", "data" = "1 Pulse (data)"),
  group_order = c("4 Pulses (A)", "3 Pulses (B)", "2 Pulses (C)", "1 Pulse (data)"),
  unit = "g",
  title = "Impact of Heat Stress Pulses on Yield",
  subtitle = "Change relative to Control baseline (0)",
  xlab = "Yield Change relative to Control",
  ylab = "Heat Treatment Level",
  sig_color = "red",
  insig_color = "green",
  conf_level = 0.95
) {
  # 1. Extract t-table from model summary
  tab <- summary(model)$tTable
  heat_rows <- tab[grepl(term_pattern, rownames(tab)), , drop = FALSE]

  if (nrow(heat_rows) == 0) {
    stop("No coefficients matching pattern '", term_pattern, "' were found in the model.")
  }

  # 2. Extract clean group names (e.g., "A", "B", "C", "data") and map to display labels
  raw_levels <- sub(term_pattern, "", rownames(heat_rows))

  mapped_labels <- if (!is.null(group_map)) {
    ifelse(raw_levels %in% names(group_map), group_map[raw_levels], raw_levels)
  } else {
    raw_levels
  }

  alpha <- 1 - conf_level

  # 3. Build plotting data frame
  plot_data <- data.frame(
    group = mapped_labels,
    estimate = heat_rows[, "Value"],
    se = heat_rows[, "Std.Error"],
    df = heat_rows[, "DF"],
    p_val = heat_rows[, "p-value"]
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      lower = estimate - qt(1 - alpha / 2, df) * se,
      upper = estimate + qt(1 - alpha / 2, df) * se,
      group = factor(group, levels = group_order),
      sig = ifelse(p_val < 0.05, "p < 0.05 (Significant)", "p ≥ 0.05 (Not Significant)"),
      label_text = paste0(round(estimate, 1), if (nzchar(unit)) paste0(" ", unit) else "")
    )

  # 4. Compute dynamic x-axis limits to prevent text label clipping across different scale types
  x_min <- min(plot_data$lower, na.rm = TRUE)
  x_max <- max(plot_data$upper, na.rm = TRUE)
  x_range <- x_max - x_min

  x_lim_lower <- x_min - (x_range * 0.28)
  x_lim_upper <- max(10, x_max + (x_range * 0.1))

  # 5. Build plot
  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = estimate, y = group, fill = sig)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_col(width = 0.55, alpha = 0.85) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), height = 0.2, color = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_text(
      aes(x = lower - (x_range * 0.02), label = label_text),
      hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 4.5, fontface = "bold"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(
      "p < 0.05 (Significant)" = sig_color,
      "p ≥ 0.05 (Not Significant)" = insig_color
    )) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(x_lim_lower, x_lim_upper)) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      x = if (nzchar(unit)) paste0(xlab, " (", unit, ")") else xlab,
      y = ylab,
      fill = "Significance"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray30", margin = margin(b = 12)),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
}

```



## Model 1: Total fruit weight

```{r total, echo=FALSE}
m_total <- lme(
  total_weight ~ year * cultivar + heat_group,
  random=~1 | pair_id,
  data=data, method="ML",
  control=lmeControl(opt="optim")
)
summary(m_total)

anova(m_total, type="marginal")

plot_heat_effects(
  model = m_total,
  title = "Impact of Heat Stress Pulses on Total Fruit Yield",
  unit = "g"
)
```

## A-data versus the common Control

In the additive models, heat_group coefficients are adjusted A-data minus Control
differences, assumed common across years and cultivars. Weights are in grams;
healthy percentage differences are in percentage points. Intervals are pointwise.
Holm p values are adjusted across the four contrasts within each response.

```{r contrasts}
models <- list(total_weight=m_total, healthy_weight=m_healthy,
               healthy_count_pct=m_count_pct, healthy_weight_pct=m_weight_pct)
effects <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(models), function(name) {
  fit <- models[[name]]
  tab <- summary(fit)$tTable
  tab <- tab[grepl("^heat_group", rownames(tab)), , drop=FALSE]
  data.frame(outcome=name,
    comparison=paste(sub("heat_group", "", rownames(tab)), "- Control"),
    estimate=tab[, "Value"],
    lower=tab[, "Value"] - qt(.975, tab[, "DF"]) * tab[, "Std.Error"],
    upper=tab[, "Value"] + qt(.975, tab[, "DF"]) * tab[, "Std.Error"],
    p_value=tab[, "p-value"],
    p_holm=p.adjust(tab[, "p-value"], method="holm"), row.names=NULL)
}))
knitr::kable(effects, digits=4)

```

```{r}
# 1. Format the 'effects' data frame for plotting
effects_plot_data <- effects %>%
  # Support column names from both base-R (lower/upper) and broom (conf.low/conf.high)
  mutate(
    ci_lower = if ("lower" %in% names(.)) lower else conf.low,
    ci_upper = if ("upper" %in% names(.)) upper else conf.high,
    p_adj    = if ("p_holm" %in% names(.)) p_holm else p_value,

    # Human-readable panel headers
    outcome_label = factor(outcome,
      levels = c("total_weight", "healthy_weight", "healthy_count_pct", "healthy_weight_pct"),
      labels = c("Total Weight (g)", "Healthy Weight (g)", "Healthy Count (%)", "Healthy Weight (%)")
    ),

    # Clean group order: data (1 pulse) at top to A (4 pulses) at bottom
    comparison_label = factor(comparison,
      levels = c("data - Control", "C - Control", "B - Control", "A - Control"),
      labels = c("data (1 Pulse)", "C (2 Pulses)", "B (3 Pulses)", "A (4 Pulses)")
    ),

    # Significance indicator after Holm correction
    sig_status = ifelse(p_adj < 0.05, "Significant (p < 0.05)", "Not Significant")
  )

# 2. Build the Multi-Panel Forest Plot
ggplot(effects_plot_data, aes(x = estimate, y = comparison_label, color = sig_status)) +
  # Reference line at 0 (No effect compared to Control)
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.8) +
  # 95% Confidence Interval error bars
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = ci_lower, xmax = ci_upper), height = 0.25, linewidth = 0.8) +
  # Point estimates
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  # Numerical text labels above points
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", estimate)),
    vjust = -0.8, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  # Facet by model outcome with independent x-axis scales (grams vs. %)
  facet_wrap(~ outcome_label, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Significant (p < 0.05)" = "#d95f02",
    "Not Significant" = "#7570b3"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Heat Treatment Effects relative to Control",
    subtitle = "Point estimates with pointwise 95% CIs across all four model outcomes",
    x = "Estimated Difference from Unheated Control",
    y = "Heat Pulse Intensity",
    color = "Holm Significance"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray30", margin = margin(b = 10)),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray92", color = NA),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```


### Does the heat response differ between cultivars?

These candidate models retain a common Control category but allow the A-data effects
to vary by cultivar. Compare fixed effects using ML; do not automatically select
a model based on one p value.



```{r cultivar-interaction}
m_total_cultivar <- update(m_total, . ~ . + heat_group:cultivar)
m_healthy_cultivar <- update(m_healthy, . ~ . + heat_group:cultivar)
m_count_pct_cultivar <- update(m_count_pct, . ~ . + heat_group:cultivar)
m_weight_pct_cultivar <- update(m_weight_pct, . ~ . + heat_group:cultivar)
m_rotten_pct_cultivar <- update(m_rotten_pct, . ~ . + heat_group:cultivar)

anova(m_total, m_total_cultivar)
anova(m_healthy, m_healthy_cultivar)
anova(m_count_pct, m_count_pct_cultivar)
anova(m_weight_pct, m_weight_pct_cultivar)
anova(m_rotten_pct, m_rotten_pct_cultivar)
```

```{r}
library(emmeans)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

plot_emmeans_by_cultivar <- function(
  model,
  x_var = "heat_group",
  facet_var = "cultivar",
  x_order = c("Control", "data", "C", "B", "A"),
  x_labels = c("Control (0)", "data (1 Pulse)", "C (2 Pulses)", "B (3 Pulses)", "A (4 Pulses)"),
  title = "Fruit Response to Heat Pulses by Cultivar",
  subtitle = "Interaction model adjusted means ± 95% CI",
  xlab = "Heat Treatment Scheme",
  ylab = "Adjusted Weight",
  unit = "g",
  base_size = 13
) {
  # 1. Construct formula dynamically (~ x_var | facet_var)
  emm_formula <- as.formula(paste("~", x_var, "|", facet_var))

  # 2. Extract EMMs as a data frame
  emm_df <- as.data.frame(emmeans(model, emm_formula))

  # 3. Dynamic CI column detection (handles lower.CL/upper.CL or asym.LCL/asym.UCL)
  lower_col <- names(emm_df)[grep("lower|LCL", names(emm_df), ignore.case = TRUE)][1]
  upper_col <- names(emm_df)[grep("upper|UCL", names(emm_df), ignore.case = TRUE)][1]

  emm_df$lower_ci <- emm_df[[lower_col]]
  emm_df$upper_ci <- emm_df[[upper_col]]

  # Assign standardized variables for plotting
  emm_df$x_val <- emm_df[[x_var]]
  emm_df$facet_val <- emm_df[[facet_var]]

  # 4. Reorder and relabel X-axis factor levels logically
  if (!is.null(x_order)) {
    existing_levels <- levels(factor(emm_df$x_val))
    valid_order <- intersect(x_order, existing_levels)

    if (length(valid_order) > 0) {
      emm_df$x_val <- factor(emm_df$x_val, levels = valid_order)
      if (!is.null(x_labels) && length(x_labels) == length(valid_order)) {
        levels(emm_df$x_val) <- x_labels
      }
    }
  }

  # 5. Build ggplot
  y_title <- if (nzchar(unit)) paste0(ylab, " (", unit, ")") else ylab

  ggplot(emm_df, aes(x = x_val, y = emmean, group = facet_val, color = facet_val)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower_ci, ymax = upper_ci), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~ facet_val) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      x = xlab,
      y = y_title
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
    )
}
```

)
```

)

## Intensity comparisons: A-data

A, B, C and data correspond to 4, 3, 2 and 1 heat pulses.
Weight outcomes use the cultivar-interaction models; percentage outcomes use
additive models. Means are averaged equally over years (and cultivars for
percentage outcomes). Controls remain pooled within each year and cultivar.
Comparisons use Holm correction for the six A-data pairs within each outcome/cultivar;
confidence intervals are pointwise 95%, not simultaneous. Degrees of freedom
use a conservative minimum over the fixed coefficients involved.

```{r intensity-helper}
# No additional packages are required.
intensity_results <- function(fit, cultivar_level=NULL) {
  grid <- expand.grid(
    year=levels(data$year),
    cultivar=if (is.null(cultivar_level)) levels(data$cultivar) else cultivar_level,
    heat_group=levels(data$heat_group)
  )
  grid$year <- factor(grid$year, levels=levels(data$year))
  grid$cultivar <- factor(grid$cultivar, levels=levels(data$cultivar))
  grid$heat_group <- factor(grid$heat_group, levels=levels(data$heat_group))
  X <- model.matrix(delete.response(terms(formula(fit))), grid)
  X <- X[, names(fixef(fit)), drop=FALSE]
  mean_X <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(data$heat_group), function(g) {
    colMeans(X[grid$heat_group == g, , drop=FALSE])
  }))
  rownames(mean_X) <- levels(data$heat_group)

  estimate_contrast <- function(L) {
    estimate <- as.numeric(L %*% fixef(fit))
    se <- sqrt(as.numeric(L %*% vcov(fit) %*% L))
    df <- min(fit$fixDF$X[abs(L) > 1e-10])
    data.frame(estimate=estimate, SE=se, df=df,
      lower=estimate-qt(.975,df)*se,
      upper=estimate+qt(.975,df)*se,
      p_value=2*pt(-abs(estimate/se),df))
  }
  means <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rownames(mean_X), function(g) {
    cbind(group=g, estimate_contrast(mean_X[g, ]))
  }))
  # Pairwise comparisons ONLY among heated groups.
  pairs <- combn(c("A", "B", "C", "data"), 2, simplify=FALSE)
  comparisons <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pairs, function(g) {
    cbind(comparison=paste(g, collapse=" - "),
      estimate_contrast(mean_X[g[1], ] - mean_X[g[2], ]))
  }))
  comparisons$p_holm <- p.adjust(comparisons$p_value, method="holm")
  list(means=means, comparisons=comparisons)
}

# A-data scheme effects relative to the common Control can also be compared
# by subtracting each scheme's mean_X row from another, as above:
# (A - Control) - (B - Control) = A - B.
```

```{r intensity-tables-plots, results='asis', fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
intensity_models <- list(
  total_weight=m_total_cultivar,
  healthy_weight=m_healthy_cultivar,
  healthy_count_pct=m_count_pct,
  healthy_weight_pct=m_weight_pct
)
intensity_export <- list()

for (outcome in names(intensity_models)) {
  fit <- intensity_models[[outcome]]
  is_weight <- outcome %in% c("total_weight", "healthy_weight")
  groups <- if (is_weight) levels(data$cultivar) else "Both cultivars"
  for (g in groups) {
    result <- intensity_results(fit, if (is_weight) g else NULL)
    cat("\n\n### ", outcome, ": ", g, "\n\n", sep="")
    # A mean-vs-zero p value is not relevant here, so omit it.
    print(knitr::kable(result$means[c("group","estimate","SE","lower","upper")],
      digits=2, caption="Adjusted means and pointwise 95% confidence intervals"))
    cat("\n\n")
    print(knitr::kable(result$comparisons, digits=4,
      caption="A-data comparisons; negative estimates mean the first group is lower"))
    cat("\n\n")

    # Order the plot by pulse count: Control, data, C, B, A.
    z <- result$means[match(c("Control","data","C","B","A"),result$means$group), ]
    plot(0:4, z$estimate, type="b", pch=19, xaxt="n",
      ylim=range(z$lower,z$upper), xlab="Heat pulses",
      ylab=if (is_weight) "Adjusted weight (g)" else "Adjusted healthy percentage (%)",
      main=paste(outcome,g))
    axis(1, at=0:4, labels=c("Control","data: 1","C: 2","B: 3","A: 4"))
    arrows(0:4,z$lower,0:4,z$upper,angle=90,code=3,length=.05)
    # Lines guide the eye; the model treats pulse schemes as categories.
    intensity_export[[paste(outcome,g)]] <- list(means=result$means,
                                                comparisons=result$comparisons)
  }
}
```

Pulse timing also differs across A-data; these are scheme comparisons, not a
confirmed causal effect per additional pulse. The connecting lines do not imply
a fitted linear trend. Control has no active heating; its chamber protocol is
assumed comparable across the original intensity groups.

### Discuss
```{r}
library(emmeans)

# 1. Calculate adjusted marginal means
emms <- emmeans(m_total_cultivar, ~ heat_group | cultivar)

# 2. Pairwise comparisons among A-data (excluding Control) with Holm adjustment
pairs_AD <- contrast(emms, "pairwise", combine = TRUE, adjust = "holm") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  filter(!grepl("Control", contrast))

# 3. Plot dose-response curve
plot(emms)
```
## Diagnostics

```{r diagnostics, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
models <- intensity_models
for (name in names(models)) {
  fit <- models[[name]]
  r <- residuals(fit, type="normalized")
  par(mfrow=c(1,2))
  plot(fitted(fit), r, xlab="Fitted", ylab="Normalized residual", main=name)
  abline(h=0, lty=2)
  qqnorm(r); qqline(r)
}
par(mfrow=c(1,1))
```

These are preliminary Gaussian mixed models. Percentage responses require
particular care with residual variance, normality and predictions outside 0-100.
Consider beta-binomial (count percentage) or beta (weight percentage) models if needed.
Cultivar is confounded with field; year effects do not identify a weather or alternate-bearing mechanism.
